title: Ordered-simplex evaluation of the cone straightening
statement:
Use simplicial sets and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent realization and cosimplicial pinched cubes $Q^\bullet$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], and the cone adjunction and enriched diagram categories of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. Work in fixed universes enlarged to contain all constructions. For $n\geq0$, let $[n]$ be the ordinary category with objects $0,\ldots,n$ and one arrow $i\to j$ exactly when $i\leq j$, regarded as a discrete simplicial category. Let $a:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]^{\mathrm{op}}\to[n]^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the identity on objects, collapsing every nonempty mapping simplicial set to a point. Write $a_!$ for enriched left Kan extension, the left adjoint of restriction $a^*$, as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Define $L^{\mathrm{lin}}=a_!L_{\Delta^n}$ and $U^{\mathrm{lin}}=U_{\Delta^n}a^*$; thus $L^{\mathrm{lin}}\dashv U^{\mathrm{lin}}$ as ordinary functors. For any small simplicial set $K$, set $V(K)=\int^{[m]}K_m\times Q^m$, the quotient of $\coprod_mK_m\times Q^m$ by $(K(\alpha)z,q)\sim(z,Q(\alpha)q)$ for $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$, $z\in K_m$, $q\in Q^r$. Set $(\operatorname{Sing}_Q B)_m=\operatorname{Hom}(Q^m,B)$, so that $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$.

For every map $p:X\to\Delta^n$ and every $0\leq j\leq n$, put $X_{\geq j}=X\times_{\Delta^n}\Delta^{\{j,\ldots,n\}}$ and $X_j=X\times_{\Delta^n}\{j\}$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(j)\cong V(X_{\geq j}).$$
It is natural in $X$ over $\Delta^n$. For $j\leq k$, the diagram map $L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(k)\to L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(j)$ is the map $V(X_{\geq k})\to V(X_{\geq j})$ induced by inclusion. For any strict diagram $H:[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$, the canonical fiber isomorphism $(U^{\mathrm{lin}}H)_j\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q H(j)$ identifies the restriction to $X_j$ of the adjoint of $b:L^{\mathrm{lin}}X\to H$ with the $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ adjoint of
$$V(X_j)\longrightarrow V(X_{\geq j})\cong L^{\mathrm{lin}}X(j)\xrightarrow{b_j}H(j).$$
No fibrancy hypothesis on $X,p,H$ is imposed.
